newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to address arms, drugs during Asia trip.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to address arms, drugs during Asia trip.

text.p: Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke begins a nine-day tour of Asia on Wednesday to discuss relations between Europe and Asia, disarmament in the region, drugs, investment and high technology.
Within the framework of Belgian efforts to foster arms control, he will try and persuade India and Pakistan to give up the production of anti-personnel mines, diplomatic sources said.

Belgium has been among the frontrunners seeking a total ban on such mines, but might find it hard to convince both countries, which says they need the devices to defend their borders, to end production, the sources said.
In Singapore, the Belgian minister will take part in the February 13 and 14 meeting of the Association of southeast Asian nations (ASEAN) with the European Union.

Derycke will be in New Delhi on February 16 and 17 for the first visit by a Belgian foreign minister since 1981, and from there he will travel to Bangalore for a one-day visit to local information technology and other hi-tech companies.
In Bombay on February 19 Derycke will visit the diamond trade and the port.
India is Belgium's main Asian trading partner with diamond trade between Antwerp and Bombay -- a main centre for cutting and polishing -- taking up the bulk of the action.

During his February 19 and 20 visit Derycke will address drug-trafficking with Pakistan, which is frequently used for shipments of narcotics from Afghanistan, the sources said. He will also be the first foreign minister to meet the new government after last Monday's elections.
Derycke returns to Belgium on February 21.
